hyps.why: At very small learning rates the model is undertrained within 243 epochs, so raising the rate helps a lot, whereas at high rates it does not.
Learning rates near 0.278-1 make Adam diverge, so stepping up further hurts more than it does elsewhere.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training at aggressive learning rates.
With a tiny learning rate, fewer update steps from larger batches leaves the model more undertrained.
Deeper networks are more unstable at high learning rates, so adding layers hurts more.
Wider layers amplify update magnitudes at high learning rates, causing instability.
Strong L2 penalty near alpha=1 over-regularizes and underfits, while small alpha changes do nothing.
Small batches with large learning rates give noisy, unstable updates, so raising the rate hurts more.
Large batches mean fewer steps, so a larger learning rate compensates and helps more.
When the learning rate is small, wider networks fit faster and compensate for slow training.
